stashapp/stash.body:
### Have you enabled troubleshooting mode?

- [x] I confirm that the troubleshooting mode is enabled.

### Describe the bug

The `unzipFile` method in `internal/manager/task_import.go:156` joins zip entry names directly into the extraction path without validating that the result stays within BaseDir:

    fn := filepath.Join(t.BaseDir, f.Name)

A zip entry named `../../../../arbitrary.txt` resolves to a path outside the import directory, allowing arbitrary file write. No authentication is required in the default configuration (`HasCredentials()` returns false).

A second instance exists in `pkg/pkg/manager.go:221-222` where `filepath.Clean(f.Name)` preserves leading `../` and `store.writeFile` at `pkg/pkg/store.go:106` joins it with the package directory, escaping it.

A third issue: `internal/api/routes_plugin.go:60` uses `strings.HasPrefix(dir, pluginDir)` without a trailing separator, allowing a plugin directory named `foo` to match a sibling `foobar`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start stash with default configuration (no credentials set).
2. Complete setup via the `setup` GraphQL mutation.
3. Create a zip file containing an entry with path `../../../../canary.txt`.

stashapp/stash.title: Preview generation fails when video stream has a non-zero start offset
stashapp/stash.body:
### Have you enabled troubleshooting mode?

- [x] I confirm that the troubleshooting mode is enabled.

### Describe the bug

Video preview generation fails for files whose video stream starts at a non-zero timestamp while the container reports `start: 0`.
 
Stash distributes the preview segments evenly across the duration reported by the container, so the first segment is cut at t=0. At that position no video frame exists yet and ffmpeg writes a 0-byte file. The same happens at the end, because the effective video length is shorter than the reported duration.
 
The concat demuxer determines the stream layout from the first entry of the list. With an empty file there it aborts with "Output file does not contain any stream", and the entire preview fails even though the remaining segments were encoded correctly. The fallback path fails identically.
 
Observed with HEVC files converted with HandBrake 1.11.1, but the codec is not the cause: the relevant property is the video stream start offset, which can occur with any codec or encoder. In this case HandBrake preserved an offset from the original recording, where audio started before video.

### Describe the feature you'd like

Most scrapers are URL scrapers, and the way they work is by matching whatever URL is in the field for any scene/performer/gallery/image to a pattern declared in the scraper.

The problem arises when two or more scrapers can scrape the same pattern, a situation that can occur when scrapers are consolidated into larger scrapers that can cover multiple domains because they use the same CMS or belong to the same network. A recent example would be the new MojoHost scraper introduced in [CommunityScrapers 3bdeead](https://github.com/stashapp/CommunityScrapers/commit/3bdeead917fe8650e565a5a5b13363eacc9e5c56) that moved patterns from over a dozen scrapers into one big scraper which will be easier for us maintainers to keep updated.

Users who have the old FFCSH scraper installed can install the new MojoHost scraper and suddenly their scraping of fantasyflipflop.com becomes non-deterministic because sometimes Stash will use the new MojoHost scraper and sometimes it will use the old FFCSH scraper. stashapp/stash.body:
### Have you enabled troubleshooting mode?

### Describe the bug

**Describe the bug**
Preview video generation fails for 100% of scenes in a library when using the default "Generate → Previews" task with no explicit per-task preview options — every scene fails instantly and identically, while sprite/cover/phash generation succeeds normally for the same scenes.


The fallback attempt (audio-less retry) fails identically. This reproduces on every scene tested — different codecs, containers, durations, and file sizes — ruling out a per-file issue.

mutation {

  })
}

stashapp/stash.title: Plugin settings should be able to add connect-src CSP sources
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like

Add a mechanism for plugin developers to contribute additional connect-src entries to Stash’s page Content Security Policy through plugin settings, rather than only through the static ui.csp.connect-src value in the plugin’s yml.

Currently, a plugin’s CSP contributions are hard-coded in its shipped yml file. This forces plugins that talk to a user-configurable backend to either ship a broad wildcard (e.g. http://*:7860), which is poor security policy, or require users to hand-edit the plugin’s yml on every update. A cleaner approach is to let a plugin define a settings entry whose value is treated as a validated connect-src source when building the page CSP header. Concretely: settings whose key starts with csp_ and whose value is a valid concrete http/https URL get appended to the page’s connect-src directive for that plugin.

Validation would be strict: values must be concrete http/https URLs with a host, and anything else (wildcards like http://*:7860, non-URLs, disallowed schemes, empty strings, values containing CSP meta-characters) is ignored, so invalid settings can never corrupt the header.

stashapp/stash.title: Improve dense scene marker readability
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like

Improve the Scene Player marker rendering so markers remain visually distinct when several markers are close together on the timeline.

The current colored marker UI is useful when markers are spaced out, but dense parts of a scene can become hard to read:

- Adjacent range markers with different primary tags can receive colors that look very similar, making them appear like one continuous marker
- Very short range markers can visually merge with nearby markers because the rendered marker has a minimum width that may be larger than its actual timeline span
- In these cases, users have to hover markers one-by-one to understand where one marker ends and another begins

This is a follow-up to the existing range-marker UI, not a request for a new marker type. The goal is to make the current colored marker timeline reliable in dense areas.

A good solution could include one or more of:

- choosing colors with awareness of marker proximity on the rendered timeline, not only the unique list of primary tags in the scene
- increasing perceptual contrast for adjacent or overlapping markers with different primary tags
- adding separators, outlines, or anot

stashapp/stash.title: HEIC/HEIF Image Format Support with Live Photo Pairing
stashapp/stash.body:
**Inspiring Issue:** [#4115 - Support HEIC images for photos taken on iOS devices](https://github.com/stashapp/stash/issues/4115)

## Summary

Add support for HEIC/HEIF image files, the default photo format on iOS devices since iOS 11 (2017). This RFC covers three areas:

1. **HEIC still image support**: scanning, thumbnail generation, and browser-compatible serving via pre-generated WebP conversion
2. **Live Photo pairing**: detecting and linking companion MOV video files to their HEIC still images
3. **UI integration**: scan/generate toggles following existing patterns, Live Photo playback in the image viewer

## Background

HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) uses HEVC (H.265) encoding inside an ISOBMFF container. It is the default camera format on all modern iPhones and iPads. Browser support is Safari-only due to licensing costs, so server-side conversion is needed for web serving.

### What changed since the original issue

The original 2023 issue was blocked by ffmpeg lacking HEIC support. FFmpeg 8 (late 2025) added HEVC still picture decoding, but my testing revealed that ffmpeg 8 still cannot properly handle tiled HEIC files, which are the most common format produced by

stashapp/stash.title: Reorganise generated artifacts
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like

Image thumbnails use `fsutil.GetIntraDir` to generate a segmented path for their artifacts. That is, it takes the checksum of the image and creates intermediate directories of the first four characters of that checksum to place the artifact file.

For example, an image with checksum `0039dee44b30846756b01f89f642fb5a` would have its thumbnail file generated as: `00/39/0039dee44b30846756b01f89f642fb5a_640.jpg`.

This system should be extended to our other generated artifacts, or we should consider other ways to organise them (perhaps in concert with work on #5094).

The simplest way forward is to adapt the segmented path naming for the following generated artifacts:
- marker previews (under `generated/markers`)
- video previews (under `generated/screenshots`)
- vtt sprite files (under `generated/vtt`)
- interactive heatmaps (under `generated/interactive_heatmaps`)
- transcode files (under `generated/transcodes`)

This could be done automatically for newly generated artifacts, with an optional migration to move existing artifacts into their segmented directories. Code that uses the artifacts could check the legacy location as a fallback.

stashapp/stash.title: SQL Query Improvments for Larger DB
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like

Currently, there are some edge case issue for larger databases. 

The main conversation for it starts on Discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/559159668438728723/559159931505213440/1453045631370395659)

My proposed fixes/helps are on Discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/559159668438728723/559159931505213440/1453197001490567410)

Current Behavior:

  When filtering scenes by folder path (e.g., /data/namer/), Stash builds a query like:
```
  SELECT DISTINCT scenes.id
  FROM scenes
  LEFT JOIN scenes_files ON scenes_files.scene_id = scenes.id
  LEFT JOIN files ON scenes_files.file_id = files.id
  LEFT JOIN folders ON files.parent_folder_id = folders.id
  ...
  WHERE (folders.path || '/' || files.basename LIKE '%/data/namer/%')
  AND (TRIM(scene_stash_ids.stash_id) = '' OR scene_stash_ids.stash_id IS NULL)
```

  This approach has several performance issues:

  1. `LIKE '%pattern%'` with leading wildcard prevents SQLite from using the index on `folders.path`, forcing a full table scan

  2. String concatenation `(folders.path || '/' || files.basename)`  must be computed for every row

  3. `TRIM()` function call prevents index usage and

stashapp/stash.title: Improving pagination performance by caching results of larger queries
stashapp/stash.body:
Spinning off my comment from #6319 since that issue has been closed.

Core problem: Pagination in tabs with lots of results can be very slow. Every page access requires performing the full query. This results in sorting p*(p+1)/2 * perPage records rather than the minimum required perPage * p when paginating through p pages.

### Steps to reproduce

Here's an example from my setup with 1.7M images:
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=00002 **2.6s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=00020 **2.9s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=00200 **3.2s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=02000 **6.1s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=20000 **19s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=40000 **22.8s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=20&p=80000 **22.8s**

Now consider this query that essentially caches 100 of the previous queries for a memory cost of roughly 117 kB:
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=2000&p=002 **3.6s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=2000&p=020 **6.5s**
https://localhost:9999/images?sortby=path&perPage=2000

stashapp/stash.title: Support for scanning Encryped Archives
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, Stash does not support scanning encrypted archives that require a password.
I have some torrent files that I need to continue seeding, and extracting them manually would consume a lot of disk space unnecessarily.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like Stash to support reading passwords from `.password` files when scanning encrypted archives. Here are two proposed formats:

1. Per-file password:

```
A.zip
A.password
B.7z
B.password
```

2. Per-folder password:

```
foo.password
foo/
├── a.zip
├── b.zip
```

In this case, all encrypted archives inside the `foo/` folder would use `foo.password` for decryption.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Using external scripts to extract the archives before scanning.

stashapp/stash.title: Upgrade React + Dependencies
stashapp/stash.body:
# Upgrade React v17.0.2 → 18.x.x

### Scope
The version of React used by Stash was released [4 years ago](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#1702-march-22-2021). Since then two major new versions have been released. The React ecosystem has mostly moved on from version 17, with 18 most commonly listed as the minimum.

##  Long Form
I imagine there'll come a point where upgrading React will need to take place. I'm kicking things off by making this issue.

## Examples
While developing a UI plugin, I found that many third-party libraries were incompatible with the current version of React used by Stash. I've had to re-implement a lot of functionality that I otherwise wouldn't have to if Stash were using a later version.

## Reference Reading
- [How to upgrade to React 18](https://react.dev/blog/2022/03/08/react-18-upgrade-guide)

This has the affect of reducing the available content area available for elements on the page to render, but most notable is the abrupt cutoff of the top navigation bar as its width hits the invisible margins imposed by the browser.

## To reproduce

2. Notice the layout abnormalities

For pure aesthetic reasons, it'd be nice to have the top bar extend all the way to edge of the screen.

stashapp/stash.body:

Since most objects in stash can have multiple URLs now it would be good to not just rely on the index of the of a given URL to determine the "Primary" URL of an object. 

### **Describe the solution you'd like**
Stash-box handles this well by classifying specific URLs based on patterns. I suggest lifting that approach into Stash itself and potentially expanding on it by allowing studios to define their own URL patterns. This would enable Stash to determine a "Primary" URL for an object when it has multiple URLs and an assigned studio, by applying the studio's specified patterns. Additionally, integrating URL classifications could open the door for configuration options where users can specify which types of URLs they want to pull during a Scrape, Tagger, or Identify operation

going into individual objects that have multiple URLs and reordering them so the primary URL is in the first position or otherwise iterating over all URLs looking for a specific one

stashapp/stash.title: Include settings when executing plugin task
stashapp/stash.body:
# Include settings when executing plugin task

### Scope
While scoping the development of an embedded JavaScript plugin, I was surprised to learn that a plugin's settings aren't available within the plugin's runtime environment by default. Instead, it seems the only way to access these settings is to make a GraphQL query.

##  Long Form
It seems logical to me that a plugin's settings exist because they'll in some way affect the execution of whatever the plugin is doing. Not making these settings available immediately seems counterintuitive and necessities making an HTTP request when the settings could be provided alongside other important parameters such as `input.Args`.

## Examples
The runtime environment currently provides `input` as a global variable. I propose that this be extended to include a key for `settings`.

## Reference Reading
- https://github.com/stashapp/stash/blob/c5fe6748c08b63dcb457db53920e9edbe2b9fa6a/pkg/plugin/js.go#L62-L68

stashapp/stash.title: Support hardware acceleration for phash/sprite/preview generation tasks
stashapp/stash.body:
On the back of multiple other issues, a generic issue to encompass and link all generate hwaccel issues and proposals

In-depth testing done here: https://git.feederbox.cc/feederbox826/5731-hwaccel

# tl;dr
- VAAPI decode is *fast* and accounts for most of the speed increase
- VAAPI can return a vmaf of ~95 compared to libx264
- QSV-hybrid's speed increase is not worth the complications
- VAAPI usertime improvements
  - up to 15x for single sprite
  - up to 45x for hw-decode previews
  - up to 70x for hw-full-pipe previews

NVENC cannot seek without loading everything previously in the file (not even into GPU memory). This results in times closer to 10s seek -> +1s exec

On the side of NVENC, this can lead to times of up to 1.8x libx264 on a Ryzen 3600 even when running from RAMDisk and piping into NUL

Enabling memory limit configuration would prevent OOM kills, ensuring smoother operation during media generation. This would enhance reliability and stability, particularly over extended periods of usage, allowing users to work without interruption due to memory issues.

At the moment, there is no effective method to restrict memory usage, as the process continues to consume memory until it reaches the set limit, leading to potential crashes.

This issue has been observed over the past three days of generating media, as illustrated in the attached image, where green represents Stash's increasing memory usage over time. I have already gradually increased the maximum memory from 1 GiB to 5 GiB and now to 10 GiB, but the problem persists. This is occurring on Kubernetes with the latest version on an ARM64 mach

stashapp/stash.title: Hardware decoding in generation tasks
stashapp/stash.body:

stashapp/stash.title: Image relationships feature to allow linking related images
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
There are a few situations where being able to specify a relationship between two images may be desirable:
- An image is an upscale of another
- An image is a decensored version of another (e.g. JAV or hentai)
- An image is a modified version of an original for fetish purposes (captions, pixelated images, photoshops)
- An image clip has had audio added to it (common for animated media that later have voices/sfx added by 3rd parties)
- The images are related, but do not fit the definition of a gallery, or there are too few images to warrant a gallery (small groups of images belonging to one post of a creator)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a 'Relationships' field to images. This field allows specifying one more related images. Allow specifying a string to describe what is distinct about each image ('Original', 'Decensored').

In terms of UI, it may make sense to put the relationships into its own tab, similar to how Markers are for Scenes. The icons could potentially take up a lot of vertical space, cluttering the Details tab.

stashapp/stash.title: Add new /temp/ Application Path instead of using /generated/temp/ for temporary files
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
During content generation, the path /generated/tmp/ is used.
I have an Unraid NAS server with SSD drives setup as its "Cache" in addition to its standard disk "Array".
I use the Array for my /generated/ path.  This works well as once the content has been generated, there is no reason to use the more efficient (but smaller sized) Cache.  But for /generated/tmp/ using the Array is not as performant and causes more wear and tear on my spinning disks, vs. a path that is on the Cache.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A new Application Path named something like /temp/ that would be used instead of the path /generated/tmp/ (and any other paths that are used in a similar transient capacity, if there are any others).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I cannot think of an alternative solution.  It is not a critical issue, so I have been just accepting it.

**Additional context**
I am new to stash, so I was surprised that the existing Application Path of /cache/ was not already used for temporary file purposes.  But I suppose the term "cache" can have a lot of different meanings.

The problem I want to solve isn't to remove the directories; just to clean up stash.  So adding a flag to Clean to just clean up missing directories (so there's no risk of accidentally deleting scenes) would probably be sufficient.

stashapp/stash.title: Client Side Hamming Distance Settings for Identify Tasks
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
False positives frequently occur when using the identify function with various stash-box instances.  Partly I believe this is due to some bad hashes on the stash-box side which is understandable.  False positives also seem to stem from the phash hamming distance that is set on the server side.  In my case I would only like to pull exact matches into my db when using identify.  While I understand one of the strengths of perceptual hashing is matching on images with some distance, I believe that allowing the user to decide the distance would be a better use experience.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow client side hamming distance to be set per stash-box in the identify settings.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Adding a similar setting to the ad hoc tagger settings might also be useful.  That interface feels more suited to setting varying distances as the user is validating the matches before saving in most cases.

**Additional context**
I believe fansdb recently made the server side change to increase the hamming distance from 0.  This created well over 1000 false positives in a sin

stashapp/stash.title: Edit Modal - Improving bulk editing workflow
stashapp/stash.body:
## Summary
This RFC proposes a UI/UX change to the bulk editing workflow of multiple items/objects (i.e. Scenes) and their multi-field input values on the Edit modal windows. To replace the current method of using tabs with a simpler, less redundant, and more commonly used system that will improve familiarity with the workflow.

## Current Workflow
At present, the bulk editing of multiple Scenes' multi-field input values uses tabs atop each field. Users must select one of three tabs to inform how they will manipulate the input values:

`Overwrite` all values.
`Add` new values.
`Remove` existing values

The functionality of this approach is inefficient, as only one of the three functions can be utilized per input field at a time. This layout may also be confusing to some users, as I do not think it's a generally adopted approach for UIUX.

## Proposed Workflow
The new workflow would use a more intuitive and commonly adopted method to manipulate multiple values of multiple items simultaneously. This is done by displaying checkbox states (`checked`, `unchecked`, `intermediate`) adjacent to each respective input value.

As in Windows, and other operating systems and brow

After progressing from this modal, the second modal window presents the *Destination* fields first (left column) and the *Source* fields second (right column).

I strongly suspect if two advanced contributors often find this confusing, it isn't unlikely that other users may get confused.

Additionally, there is a lack of helper text to guide users on the role of each field.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

**Describe the solution you'd like**

stashapp/stash.title: Multiple image support for all objects using corresponding user-defined image attributes
stashapp/stash.body:
## Yet another multiple image support request
We've received numerous feature requests (FRs) for multiple image support across various objects, including performers, alternate scene covers (scenes), DVD/CD/VHS covers and spines for movies (now groups), and studio favicons (studios). Many of these FRs have been limited in scope or overly simplistic. For instance, some requests specify a single image type (e.g., DVD Spine Cover) hardcoded to a movie objects, while others propose multiple image support without any corresponding metadata/attributes, effectively creating a redundant sub-gallery of images outside existing only within an object.

## Proposal: One multiple image support request to rule them all
To address these needs comprehensively, I propose we implement multiple image support for all objects (scenes, performers, studios, tags, groups) using corresponding user-defined custom image types. These user-defined attributes will categorize the images, allowing for diverse applications beyond mere archival purposes.

Object|(Custom) Description|(Custom, Optional) Aspect Ratio|Hardcoded

Studio|Favicon|1:1|True

A master toggle switch to disable all plugins and re-enable the prior state of all plugins (acting more like a pause state). This is going to be very useful when the user needs to troubleshoot.

stashapp/stash.title: Add data-values attributes to div.scene-specs-overlay span elements; add span.overlay-duration class; report framerate shorthand
stashapp/stash.body:
The reported video data within `div.scene-specs-overlay` could still use a bit of polishing, including the addition of displaying overlay framerate appended to the resolution to complete the resolution and framerate shorthand that's now commonly used.

1. Duration still requires its own span element and class, `<span class="overlay-duration">` so it can be properly styled
2. Each span element within `div.scene-specs-overlay` could get a data-value attribute. This will let devs/users manipulate the element based on its value
3. Add framerate shorthand in this section (only two additional characters), where resolution and framerate shorthand is just the framerate (always rounded up to the nearest integer) appended to the resolution with no spaces.

E.g. of resolution and framerate shorthand:

- 1080p60
- 1080p50
- 1080p30
- 1080p25
- 1080p24

Basic hypothetical CSS
```css
.overlay-framerate {
    display: none; /* hide the framerate by default */
}

.overlay-framerate[data-value="50"],
.overlay-framerate[data-value="60"],
.overlay-framerate[data-value="100"],
.overlay-framerate[data-value="120"] {
    display: contents; /* show only high framerates */
}

``

stashapp/stash.title: Support for galleryByQueryFragment for image galleries
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like
I’d like to enable scraping `galleryByQueryFragment` for image galleries. This feature would allow scene metadata to be applied to galleries, even when the corresponding scene is not present in one's Stash instance.

### Describe the benefits this would bring to existing users
Enabling scrape queries for galleries would streamline the process of updating gallery metadata and save users time by eliminating the need to manually copy data from the relevant Stash Box after a search. This enhancement would improve user efficiency and overall experience.

### Is there an existing way to achieve this goal?
Currently, I can use the 'Copy from Scene' plugin for galleries with matching scenes. However, for galleries without a matching scene, I cannot use scrape queries. While I can reference scene names in the absence of matching PHashes, galleries do not currently support scrape queries.

### Additional context
This is not a request for gallery hash support, as has been requested elsewhere. The goal is specifically to integrate scrape queries into gallery management.

stashapp/stash.title: Scrapers that build a queryURL
stashapp/stash.body:
There are several niggling issues with scrapers that build a queryURL in order to provide `scrapeByFragment` functionality and in aggregate this is creating a poor user experience.

For this example we can use the following scraper:
```yml
name: StudioX
sceneByURL:
  - action: scrapeXPath
    url:
      - studiox.com/update
    scraper: sceneScraper
sceneByFragment:
  action: scrapeXPath
  queryURL: "{url}"
  scraper: sceneScraper
xPathScrapers:
  sceneScraper:
    scene:
      Title:
        fixed: Example scraper
```

The implicit requirements for this scraper mean that a scene needs to:
- Have an URL _saved to the scene_
- That URL needs to be _the first URL_
- The URL needs to match the pattern of the `sceneByURL` action

If the user is not aware of these requirements and fails to meet them, Stash will either show the cryptic error `scraper StudioX: Get "%7Burl%7D": unsupported protocol scheme` (if the URL is missing) or give a false positive with a green notification that says `No scenes found` (if the URL does not match, or the matcing URL is not the first one).

To reproduce this we can create an empty scene and:
- select StudioX from the "Scrape

stashapp/stash.title: Multiple image support for tags
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently each performer and tag has a single set image (static or animated) that doesn't change.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I request for an ability to have multiple photos for each performer/tag so that on each visit of the Performers or Tags page, a new image is shown from a set of x images for that particular performer or tag.

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to filter Groups by Alias
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently there's no option to filter Groups by their Aliases, even though filters for every other field of a Group exists.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add the option to filter Groups by Aliases. As the field takes in string values, the filter options like in Synopsis would be helpful, where you have options such as: is, is not, includes, excludes, etc.

stashapp/stash.title: Run backup as a queued task
stashapp/stash.body:
Currently, if you're running any tasks (scanning, auto tag, etc.) when you click the Backup button it runs concurrently. Expected behavior is that it would be added to the queue.

I brought this up in Discord, and @DingDongSoLong4 mentioned:

```Yeah backups aren't "queued"
I think the reason is simply because of the "Download backup" option, which needs to retrieve the download link as the "result" of the backup task, but given that tasks are run asynchronously (in the background) you can't really retrieve a task's "result".
It should probably be queued though, to be consistent with the other tasks - so we'd need to figure out a way for a task to return a "result", or retrieve the download link in some other way.```

stashapp/stash.title: Auto-save metadata fields that already include a confirmation
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Manually adding a tag to a scene already requires quite a few clicks. There is already a feature to auto-save when changing toggles from the Settings page. Using this auto-save feature for adding Tags to a scene would reduce the work required to manually add a tag to a scene.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Under the Details tab on the Scene viewer, there is a dropdown to select new tags to add. Typing a tag name is not enough to add it, you need to also click or press enter, thus confirming that the tag name is what you want.

Even this confirmation is not enough, however - accepting a tag simplify activates a Save button back at the top that must be clicked to actually save the new tag. 

This second step could be replaced with the same auto-save behavior from the settings page.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A separate top-level tagging flow that pops up suggestions and allows the user to add tags easily.

**Additional context**
![image](https://github.com/stashapp/stash/assets/109107476/51acbbc6-50ac-484c-813b-dccc18b5965b)
![image](https://github.com/stashapp/stash/assets/1091

stashapp/stash.title: Add transformational filters to images
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
With [better support for images and galleries](https://discord.com/channels/559159668438728723/1161028708874858616) on some of our minds, I'd like the same sort of adjustments as are possible for video (rotation, brightening/darkening, etc.) to be available for images.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
After #4345 is implemented, make the scene video filter settings equally available for images. There isn't much point in this until the settings can be persisted.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I haven't considered other approaches, and can't think of any.

**Additional context**
[This was first proposed in Discord.](https://discord.com/channels/559159668438728723/1161028708874858616/1181713903093301268)

stashapp/stash.title: Renaming and presentation of all tagging/scraper components and related labels
stashapp/stash.body:
### Scope
To enhance the user-friendliness of all tag related component labels and presentation.

## Goals
- Concise and relevant labels a non-technical user would understand
- Avoid technical jargon such as "fragment" and "scrape"
- Mitigate ambiguous strings and presentation
- Enhance the labels with icons when appropriate

## Items of interest
This RFC will consider the efficacy of the following labels, strings, and icons
- `Scrape All`
- `Tagger`
- Tagger `tags` icon
- `Scrape with...`
- `Scrape by Fragment`
- `Scraper Query`
- `Scene Scrape Results`
- `Identify`
- `Auto Tag`
- Scrape with `spyglass` icon
- Unrelated to the above tagging related components but possibly contributing to confusion is the word `Tags` found in the nav bar and throughout Stash
 
## Proposal
To ELI5 the goals of the above functions we could accurately say they all share the same purpose: to **import metadata**.

These functions **import metadata** in different ways, from parsing predefined keywords in a filenames (*Auto Tag*) to perceptually analyzing content and matching hashes with corresponding content on a stash box (*Scrape by Fragment*, etc). Some of these processes are

stashapp/stash.title: Make "exclusions" regex field with more user friendly UI
stashapp/stash.body:
The Exclusions edit popup (on Settings > Library > Exclusions) prompts you to enter a regex pattern to determine excluded content on Scans and Cleans. The related documentation page shows the current process: [Exclude File Configuration](https://docs.stashapp.cc/beginner-guides/exclude-file-configuration/)

Regex is not user friendly and can be difficult to get right, so I propose a more user-friendly popup where a user can enter the file or folder path to exclude, and then Stash will automatically translate that into regex as needed, behind the scenes.

For example, a popup with a text field could include a few buttons like the following:
- Directory begins with
- Directory ends with
- File begins with
- File ends with

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

stashapp/stash.title: Add dedicated page that tracks Watch History

Currently the scenes have a view counter, but no watch history is logged

This request was created as a branch / disambiguation of: #4221

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to move queued tasks up/down to change priority
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When longer running tasks like a scan are running, I have to wait for it to complete before generating a cover for a single scene from the scene edit screen, for example.

Waiting for a quick task to complete while it is being blocked by a much longer task is quite frustrating.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Tasks should get a "priority" where tasks that could be done very quickly can "jump the queue" and get processed without being blocked by a "background task".

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another option would be to implement multiple queues, e.g. system/background and user, or allow manual reordering of the current queue.

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to change default live transcode method
stashapp/stash.body:

My WMV files seek and load faster when using DASH/HLS instead of the default mp4 live transcode

**Describe the solution you'd like**
 A way to set the default transcode or reorder the list in the player.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
 I checked the yaml config file as well and couldn't find anything.

stashapp/stash.title: Filter to exclude by duration in scene duplicate checker
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I've noticed most of the mega-groups of false positives are for videos that are shorter than ~10 seconds.

I also see that you can filter with the difference by a fixed value but that leads to another observation. The maximum value 10 seconds is not enough because, unfortunately, some of my videos have an 1 minute ad that plays at the beginning and end of the video and I'd like to purge these vids as I find better versions. Maybe a percentage of the length of the video instead because in my example those 2 minutes of ads adds 8% to the length of a ~25 minute video. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

1. A setting to discard videos that are less than a certain length (in this case 10 seconds)
2. A percentage value for video length difference

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I use an external application called VDF (video duplicate finder) because it has a % video length and other filtering features but it is not as accurate as your implementation.

stashapp/stash.title: Allow user to define a custom start/end time per scene

- Always start at [xx:xx]
- Always end at [xx:xx]

Additionally, a checkbox at the start of each line should enable or disable these options.

### Describe the benefits this would bring to existing users
This feature would enhance user experience by allowing for more precise playback of scenes. stashapp/stash.title: Support HEIC image format
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Stash does not support `.heic` image files at all, which are commonly used when taking photos on iOS devices. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`.heic` images should be added as images, similar to other image formats like `.png` or `.jpg`. Previews should be generated as for any other supported image format. Since most web browser do not support `.heic` files out of the box, those files need to be converted to a broadly adapted image format when displaying them in full resolution. To save storage, `.heic` files should be converted to another images format like `.png` on the fly and in memory from the stash server when serving the image data to the front end.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
`.heic` files can also be so called "live photos", which means, that the files does contain an embedded video data of a few seconds as well. Being also able to somehow view this video in the front end would be nice, but definitely optional. Being able to display the image data should be the main focus.

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to generate scene markers immediately after creation
stashapp/stash.body:
In its current state, Stash requires that a user manually run a generate task on the entire db, or manually start a generate task specifically on that scene in order to generate the animated webp for a given marker. 

This two step process isn't terribly intuitive.
I propose that Stash just start generation of a marker as soon as the user defines where the marker is located.

There's an existing GQL mutation (`sceneMarkerCreate`) that could be modified to have an option to specify whether or not the webp should be generated. Setting this value to default to "false" would help avoid any issues with existing plugins.

Given the direct user impact, I would prefer this feature be added as a core functionality rather than a plugin.
Link to a short relevant RFC on discord here (https://discord.com/channels/559159668438728723/559399634318131210/1142009881847676959)

Thanks! 🙂

stashapp/stash.title: Allow selective tasks input to parse delineated list of directories
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have a large library, so I rarely do an entire library scan or auto-tag. The way I currently add new content is by running a script that autosorts new videos into folders, e.g. [Disney] Movie1 (1080p) into /data/Studios/Disney and [UnkownStudio] Brad Pitt - Movie2 into /data/Actors/Brad Pitt. The script then outputs the paths so I can paste them into Selective Scan and Selective Auto Tag. This can end up being a lot of copying and pasting with even a few new videos. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice if Selective Scan and Selective Auto Tag would accept multiple folders at once, delineated somehow. For example, rather than pasting `/data/Studios/Disney`, hitting the plus, pasting `/data/Actors/Brad Pitt`, hitting the plus, and then hitting the confirm; I would just paste: `/data/Studios/Disney; /data/Actors/Brad Pitt`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is simply using the tools as they currently exist (adding one folder at a time).

**Additional context**
It's a minor QoL update for a specific use case but I'm hoping this would benefit others as well.

stashapp/stash.title: Checking for StashID in scene duplicate checker
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, just the phash is used for finding duplicates but this doesn’t work all the time. Scenes with the same StashID are duplicates as well, which partly have quite different phashes.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A checkmark in the duplicate checker tool, which filters by stashid instead of the phash

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An extension, which adds tags to the duplicate candidates

stashapp/stash.title: Sync or Export/Import across devices
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

If I have 2 separate stash apps running on different computers (1 a local windows pc, 1 a remote Linux server with stash docker) there's no way to sync them so previews, performers, scenes etc are not duplicated as it is mentioned at the start of setup that keeping the DB on a non-local computer is not recommended. Did a search in discord and there was some mention of doing a export/import but when I try doing a export there's no zip file saved that can be imported in the other stash DB.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way to export everything from 1 stash install and then import into another stash instance which is platform agnostic. Incremental exports/imports from a particular date onwards would be even better.

Thanks

stashapp/stash.title: Associate audio files used by e-stim toys to matching scenes
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Videos that support "e-stim" toys often have an .mp3 soundfiles with the same name as the video, exactly like funscripts.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Stash should associate these mp3 files bearing the same name as the video, à la it does with funscripts.

Despite the fact that Stash doesn't support audio files (https://github.com/stashapp/stash/issues/11), it should still link the mp3 internally to the relevant scene in some way.

The benefit of this is that organization of files works seamlessly -- if a file is moved or deleted, Stash moves or deletes this related file. I believe Stash already handles external subtitle files in this way. In the future, this would also make it easier for related development (analyzing the mp3 to make similar heatmaps for example) -- but just having automatic name-based association should be very useful for estim users, otherwise these mp3 files can get left behind/disorganized when doing operations in Stash.

stashapp/stash.title: Filter for Is Image Clip: True/False
stashapp/stash.body:

Outside of tagging them, theres not a good way of filtering in/out the new image clips with existing image filters.

bottom text

Recognize and load more than 1 Funscript file with axis descriptors. Translate into the T-Code used by the OSR2 and SR6. Connect and control the aforementioned devices through a serial connection. Have sliders to adjust min and max movement.

There are other projects that have done the base work, but are a lot more cumbersome to use than Stash. (MultiFunPlayer for multi axis + VR. XTPlayer for standard video. Ayva Stroker uses web based UI and connects through serial (https://www.ayva-stroker-lite.io/)

**Additional context**
This is likely to be enough work to be a bounty, but I don't even know where to start.

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to favorite scenes, images and galleries
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently only performers can be marked as favourites.  It's a one-click solution fast, easy to do and quite convenient, and doesn't even requires you to open the edit page. Why don't implement the same feature for galleries, images and scenes? I know that scenes has rating, wich is somewhat similar, but it requires to go to edit mode.

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to merge details on individual fields in Scene Scrape Results dialog
stashapp/stash.body:
While Tagger and Identify allow merging, the stock UI during scraping does not.
So if you have existing tags or performers, your choice is A (old) or B (new), but
not A+B... The only way to add older items is to manually add A's items to B, then save.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A merge button for each field this makes sense for, with a setting to merge by default.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As mentioned, either manually copy, or use Tagger/etc instead. 

**Additional context**
Now that multiple URLs are possible, and scraping each is possible, the problem is enhanced.  Scrape Url1, and you've populate each field.  Now scrape Url2, and there is no easy way to 'add' results, only ignore or override.  A merge option would fix this.
Example usage: URL1 yields 3 tags, URL2 yield another (different) 5 tags.  We need a way to easily keep all 8 tags.  Ditto for performers, etc.

**Discord discussion:**

Me: is this on the dev radar?  Is there an issue/bounty for it?

Basically right now, the standard UI dialog is choose A or B for each field value.   Merge button (per field) would combine both.  Or yes, maybe it could be a default for multival

stashapp/stash.title: Hide header and footer inside lightbox by default
Add a flag to hide individual images on specific galleries

Some gallery sets have images that while are part of the release you may not want to see when viewing a gallery, i.e. contact-sheets, clean covers, blurry images, partially broken images, unnecessary images (like just a car, a forest, ...  with no performers),  etc.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way to check the image as hidden. It would indexed in the database and still appear in "images" as usual, but galleries, by default, would not show images tagged as hidden.

Maybe there could be a toggle to show/hide the hidden images while in gallery view

Stash should recognize, when a gallery changes from zipped to folder based:

stashapp/stash.title: Use videojs-vr player by default in VR tagged scenes & default videojs-vr rotation
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When opening VR-tagged videos, we have to click on the VR button, then choose 360 every single time to enable the VR player, then, we have to rotate the view 90 degrees because it's always rotated incorrectly when first enabled

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'd also like it to automatically rotate either 90 or -90 degrees so the video is rotated to face the performers, currently it's always rotated to face the middle of the video, which is not facing the performers

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Could add an option in settings to choose whether you want this automatic behaviour, or leave it off by default, in case anyone doesn't want it?

stashapp/stash.title: Option to search subfolders when generating galleries
stashapp/stash.body:
I'm working on organizing a large onlyfans library, and one thing that I am missing right now is the ability to auto-generate libraries for each performer. Right now, if you enable the automatic gallery generation feature, it will create multiple galleries per performer because many of the subfolders generated by DigitalCriminals' onlyfans scraper contain images. If, on the other hand, you leave automatic gallery generation disabled and create the `.forcegallery` file in the root of the performer's directory, no galleries are generated at all since all of the images are in subfolders.

I think a couple of good solutions here might be to add a setting for the automatic gallery generation feature that would make it either:
* automatically create at most one gallery per library, and include images detected within subfolders of that library
* enable searching subfolders for images to include in auto generated galleries when the gallery is being generated because of a  `.forcegallery` file

I realize both of these options may only really work well for the setup that I have (where I am adding each performer as a separate library manually), so I'm definitely open to other ideas as w

stashapp/stash.title: New Scene View Mode TikTok style
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like
I propose that Stash implements a new view scheme mode for scenes, similar to how TikTok displays videos or inspired by xfree.com. This mode would allow video skipping in the video queue through the scroll wheel or by swiping up or down on touch devices. The side details panel would dynamically change, facilitating seamless video skipping abilities.

### Describe the benefits this would bring to existing users
This new view mode would enhance user experience by making navigation more intuitive and fluid, enabling quicker access to videos without interruptions. Users would appreciate the convenience of both scrolling and swiping functionalities, which are widely recognized in modern video platforms.

### Is there an existing way to achieve this goal?
While the current view mode functions well, it does not offer the same level of interactivity and ease of navigation that this new scheme would provide.

### Additional context
I personally wouldn't want to see the current mode disappear with the introduction of this new view. It would be ideal to maintain both options, provided that it is easily maintainable.

stashapp/stash.title: Change O-Counter value via keybaord shortcut during video playback

stashapp/stash.title: Wrong order of images in galleries on identical files
stashapp/stash.body:

Different image galleries may have the exact same image for several reasons: 

- Two different sets of the same scenarios that share one or two images
- A gallery that is a compilation of images from other galleries

When this happens (that is: the hash is exactly the same) when viewing a gallery the images will appear out of order, so i.e. image 034 will apear before 001, 002 ....
That will also affect the image shown as cover if no cover is defined

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

2. Put images 001.jpg, 002.jpg, 003.jpg in gallery_99.zip
3. rename the previously used 003 to 006  and put it in gallery_01.zip along with images 004 and 005
4. Scan both files into the collection
5. Go to the gallery 99. It will look as 006, 001, 002

**Expected behavior**
While it is okay to get a notification that one image is in two different galleries, it should not pollute the viewing or ordering of them

stashapp/stash.title: Expand `VR tag` settings option to support multiple tags

stashapp/stash.title: Scene aliases for Performers "Jane Doe as Jane"

Ability to set an alias for a performer per scene in the same way that Stash-Box allows.

#### Areas this feature would affect

### **Additional context**

stashapp/stash.title: Display most common scene tags per performer
stashapp/stash.body:
I would like a way to see the most common tags per performer, and the most common performers per tag. Note this does NOT mean the tags assigned to the performer themselves - just the tags related to the scenes/galleries the performer appears in.

For example, the performer is in 12 outdoor scenes, 5 lesbian scenes, and 2 bedroom scenes, based on the scene tags. So in a separate tab on the performer page, I would like to see the tag cards for these in order from greatest to least. 

I would also like a way to find the performers with the most content for each given tag. For example, which performers had the most outdoor scenes, from greatest to least. Again, this does NOT mean tags assigned to the performer themselves, which is what the "Performer" tab on the Tag page is currently doing.

stashapp/stash.title: Make lightbox slideshow options aware of image clips that have duration
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Previously, images could only be static images, meaning slideshow delay is a simple matter.
Now we have clips, and clips have their own lengths that can vary.
Either we have to set the slideshow delay based on the longest clip or accept to see only the beginning of some clips.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Option to view longer clips to completion - set delay to `max(options.delay, clip.duration)`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Possible alternative: `options.delay` can be respected, but starting time for clips can be chosen randomly, so it is not only the beginning that is always played.
This seems less practical.

**Additional context**

Current options for reference:
![image](https://github.com/stashapp/stash/assets/118630824/f6ee3f0a-528d-484c-a6b0-f66e89b0f559)

Extra checkbox(es) can be added there to configure the behavior with clips.

(Related small issue: default value for the delay is set in milliseconds apparently and equals 5000, while it expects seconds and should've been 5.)

stashapp/stash.title: Distribute as Flatpak on Linux

Distribute flatpak version of stash through flathub.

stashapp/stash.title: Persistent settings/toggles via cookies
stashapp/stash.body:

**Describe the solution you'd like**

stashapp/stash.title: pHash Improvement for Short Durations
stashapp/stash.body:
##  Problem
The current phash implementation builds a collage image of 25 frames taken at regular intervals, ignoring the first and last 5% of the video. The phash of this image is then calculated and stored as the phash of the video.

This has been a successful algorithm and has allowed matching of similar videos that are not exactly the same.

However, over time it has become apparent that this algorithm is not well suited to shorter duration videos, as the frames tend to be very similar without much change between them, resulting in a collage with lots of repetition. Images with repetition like the sky or the ocean do not hash very well with phash algorithms, and end up with similar hashes.
This means many short videos end up with similar hashes, even though they are different.

##  Recommendation
I've run several tests generating more/less frames per collage, larger/smaller/portrait/landscape frames and collage, as well as switching to using a wavelet hash function.
After testing, I recommend the phash implementation is modified to take fewer frames for shorter videos, to ensure less repetition in the collage image. I suggest the following for video length x:

| Tim

Simply a "Recent Activity" sort option. Performers, studios, or tags that have had scenes/galleries/images added recently will appear before those that haven't.

Here is an example query for ordering performers by their last scenes:
```sql
SELECT p.id, p.name
FROM (SELECT performers_scenes.performer_id, MAX(scenes.date) AS latest_release_date
  FROM performers_scenes
  INNER JOIN scenes ON performers_scenes.scene_id = scenes.id
  GROUP BY performers_scenes.performer_id
) AS latest_scenes
INNER JOIN performers p
	ON p.id = latest_scenes.performer_id
ORDER BY latest_scenes.latest_release_date DESC;
```

stashapp/stash.title: Add POST support to scraper queries
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Some APIs only support API requests as POST query (e.g. [AniList](https://anilist.gitbook.io/anilist-apiv2-docs/overview/graphql/getting-started)). Currently you have to write a script scraper for those.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
In addition to `queryURL`/`queryURLReplace` add `queryBody`/`queryBodyReplace` with the same `{}` placeholder system. Since GET requests technically also allow bodies, another variable `queryHttpMethod` defaulting to `GET` can be used to differentiate between POST and GET.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Use python.

**Additional context**
Example query for AniList:
```
sceneByName:
  action: scrapeJson
  queryHttpMethod: POST
  queryURL: https://graphql.anilist.co
  queryBody: {"query":"query($title:String){Media(search:$title,type:ANIME){id,title{english,romaji},tags{name}}}","variables":{"title":{}}}
  scraper: sceneSearch

jsonScrapers:
  sceneSearch:
  ...
```
With the `{}` at the end being replaced by the search string.

stashapp/stash.title: Native Remote UI
stashapp/stash.body:
<!-- Update or delete the title if you need to delegate your title gore to something
# Native Remote UI

*### Scope*
<!-- describe the scope of your topic and your goals ideally within a single paragraph or TL;DR kind of summary so its easier for people to determine if they can contribute at a glance. -->
Web UI for a long-running application is always a bit messy because it (obviously) requires a browser to start, which is quite inconvenient in itself, and also consumes a lot more RAM and CPU than regular and well-made native applications. Ideally, web UI should only be considered as a temporary solution for rapidly deploying an application to all clients at once. For more convenience, the next step should always be a native UI for different platforms. Fortunately, Stash provides a GraphQL-based API that allows to create native external UI independently. So this is a build point for developers who would be interested in making such a native UI for Stash!

##  Long Form
<!-- Only required if your scope and titles can't cover everything. -->
There is a remote helper for Stash (https://github.com/philpw99/Stash_Helper), but it's only for a single specific platform (Windows).

stashapp/stash.title: Synology NAS and folders table
stashapp/stash.body:
**Describe the bug**
With the introduction of the 'folders' table in 0.17 (I believe), all folders under the root are added.  Synology makes hidden folders called `@eaDir` in any folder that contains one or more videos and inside that folder in a folder with the name of every video.  So if you have a folder with 100 videos in it, you get one `@eaDir` folder that has 100 folders in it, each named with the name of a video.  There is nothing in here that Stash needs or can use and no way for the user to turn this off on Synology's end.  They are only hidden in that browsing in the Synology UI they will not be displayed but they are displayed through most other protocols.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Buy the most expensive Synology NAS and max out the hard drives. (optional)
2. Run Stash via Docker on a Synology machine.
3. Scan your files and browse the 'folders' table.

**Expected behavior**
It doesn't technically hurt anything, but there will be one useless entry per video a user has on Synology systems.  This could impact performance long term, although I have no clue by how much.  Could be negligible.

# Improve filtering in presence of NULL values

### Scope

Current behavior is that there are specific conditions for NULL and there are conditions for values that ignore scenes with NULL in that field. There is no way to construct an OR query either.
There needs to be a better way to make queries on incomplete data.

One option - try to define natural behavior for queries in case of NULL. For example, "not equal X" queries should include NULL because it is not equal X.

Another option - a flag (checkbox) that would allow to specify how to treat NULL values - match or nonmatch for a particular filter that is being constructed. There is a risk of UI overload if this is going to be present when setting any filter though.

Yet another option - do nothing on individual conditions layer, improve query construction to allow grouping similar conditions with OR combinator (might be in scope of #2122).

stashapp/stash.title: Create All/New/Missing on Scene Tagger page
stashapp/stash.body:
A common request/concern from new users is:

"Wait, if I use Tagger, like you recommend, I have to click on EVERY new performer/studio/tag to add them? That will take forever, and I don't want to do that. Don't you guys have a setting to just auto add?"

Alternatives like using Identify (which can auto create, but fail to add images/etc), also fail to allow any sort of manual checking... it's basically "all or nothing".

If a "Create All" button/option is added to Tagger, most of this resistance will go away.  While there is a userscript that add 'save all' as an option, the stock app would retain the relative safety of still requiring someone to manually review, but allow them to not have to hit 'create' (and then confirm/save, so 2 clicks, plus load time) for each new performer/studio and each new tag.

Either a button (Create Missing? Create All?) or a set of options ("Create Missing Performers, Create Missing Studios, Create Missing Tags") would be good, but I'd favor the latter, as allowing partial automation... Someone might not want new tags, for example.

stashapp/stash.title: Content recommendations based on recent history
stashapp/stash.body:
Here's an idea based off a feature on a lot of tube sites: providing a page with "recommended" content from your library based on recent viewing history. This idea is different from the current filter system in the sense that it's adjusting its parameters automatically based on your recent history.

I'd imagine for Stash, the logic for serving up your library content would be primarily tag-based, with the most recently viewed tags weighted more heavily (particularly if it appears multiple times). The algorithm could also weight content by specific performers or studios if a certain one is more prominent in your history.

This feature is suggested primarily for scenes, although I suppose it could also work for galleries, images, performers, or movies depending on their tagged status.

stashapp/stash.title: Ability to to configure delay/rate limit on per scraper basis
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like
I would like the ability to specify a time period in milliseconds between individual requests when using the identify or scrape metadata features in Tagger.

### Describe the benefits this would bring to existing users
This feature would help users avoid throttling or blocking from sites that are aggressive about monitoring automated requests. By allowing control over request intervals, users can reduce the risk of being flagged as problematic, providing a smoother and more efficient experience.

### Is there an existing way to achieve this goal?
Currently, users must issue requests in small batches manually, which is not optimal and requires constant monitoring to avoid getting blocked.

### Additional context
Some sites can be particularly strict about automated requests, requiring users to be vigilant to avoid penalties. Setting a more generous interval could also benefit interactions with 'friendly' servers, allowing for a more relaxed approach to request management.

stashapp/stash.title: Query in Scene Tagger using StashID
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It appears that the Scene Tagger view does not query Stash-Boxes using attached StashIDs. The "Scrape All" button uses a fingerprint lookup (same as the "Scrape by fragment" button) whether a StashID is attached or not. The individual "Search" buttons have a configurable default under the "Query Mode" dropdown, but StashID is not one of the options. The only way to send a StashID query is to manually copy/paste it into the "Query" box yourself.

This is only an issue when you'd like to update your previously matched scenes with new data from a Stash-Box and your fingerprints match multiple entries. Otherwise, the program behaves the same way whether it's using fingerprints or StashIDs to find matches.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
At the very least, adding "StashID" as an option in the "Query Mode" dropdown of the Scene Tagger would save us the step of copying the StashID into the query field manually. It would also make sense to update the "Auto" option to add StashID as the new priority, making it StashID -> Metadata -> Filename.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The "Scrape All" button

stashapp/stash.title: Follow XDG directory specifications
stashapp/stash.body:
There was [an issue](https://github.com/stashapp/stash/issues/287) opened for this already, and it was closed because

> Let's bring the number of open issues down and close this.

The result is that stash still doesn't follow the xdg specifications three years later, thanks to the brilliance of this guy.

If the xdg folders exist and are in the environment, then the config should go to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/stash`, the database should go to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/stash`, and any non-essential data should go to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/stash`.

[XDG Base Directory Specification](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/XDG_Base_Directory)

stashapp/stash.title: Stash is unaware when an image has been replaced if the name is the same
stashapp/stash.body:
**Describe the bug**
Stash is not aware that a file has changed if the file that replaced it has the same name. I came across this when I was cleaning up some actual duplicates from a gallery, and then renamed the files to be sequentially numbered again. I had to remove all the images, scan, cleanup, and add them back to fix it.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a gallery folder name `Test`
2. add to that folder two images `image00001` and `image00002`.
3. Run scan
4. Rename `image00001` to `image00003`
5. Rename `image00002` to `image00001`
6. Run scan
7. Logs report error like: `MD5 for file /data/Galleries/Test/image00001.jpg is the same as that of /data/Galleries/Test/image00002.jpg` because it thinks `image00001` has not changed

**Expected behavior**
Stash would notice the image has been updated and scan it again to get a new MD5.

**Stash Version: (from Settings -> About):**
v0.16.0-13-g7f865096

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS 12.4
 - Browser Chrome
 - Version 103.0.5060.134

stashapp/stash.title: Inject metadata into raw streams (for external players)

Metadata is only displayed in the player if it's pre-embed in source file, but this is completely unrelated to Stash database. While #2747 is not implemented yet, it would be nice to at least view the scene name in external player.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Maybe ICY-metadata standard could be implemented for injecting metadata headers to Stash streams? 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Mounting AV directory on client to exactly the same path as than mounted on server that running Stash, and playing scenes via path instead of stream link. So at least source file name will be displayed in external player. But this method also is almost unrelated to Stash database and requires some extra preparation on client side.

**Additional context**
ICY Metadata description: https://gist.github.com/niko/2a1d7b2d109ebe7f7ca2f860c3505ef0#file-icy_meta-md

stashapp/stash.title: Jellyfin-like external remote player support
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Playing video in a browser is very inconvenient and often requires server-side transcoding, which is extremely inefficient. So native player is preferable for video playback in any case. But currently Stash provides only [raw stream links](https://github.com/stashapp/stash/pull/65) that could be played in an external player. It's better than nothing, but still not enough.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
API that would allow external players connect to Stash and wait for play command. See Jellyfin and it's remote client [jellyfin-mpv-shim](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-mpv-shim) for reference.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Opening raw stream links in your favorite native player with something like [Open With](https://github.com/darktrojan/openwith) extension. It works, but not so convenient! Scene metadata is also not sent to external players. It's also impossible to play an entire playlist at once.
* Using Stash only as scrapper tool: scrape metadata for scenes and [export is as .NFO](https://github.com/stashapp/CommunityScripts/tree/main/scripts/kodi-helper) that could be read

stashapp/stash.title: Support mobile controls inside lightbox
stashapp/stash.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like
On mobile devices, the gallery lightbox should respond to standard mobile controls, commonly referred to as "touch gestures" or "swipe navigation." Currently, Stash uses desktop image controls even in mobile format.

### Describe the benefits this would bring to existing users
Implementing these mobile controls would significantly improve the user experience by allowing for more natural and intuitive navigation. Users would be able to swipe left or right to view the previous or next image seamlessly, and zooming in would be straightforward with double-tap functionality, making the gallery more user-friendly on mobile devices.

### Is there an existing way to achieve this goal?
Currently, the functionality does not support mobile gestures; when swiping left or right, the image moves around the screen instead of transitioning to the next or previous image. Additionally, double-tapping does not control zoom and instead navigates images as per desktop controls.

### Additional context
To reproduce this issue:
- Open the gallery lightbox on a mobile device.
- Attempt to swipe left or right; the image follows the user’s finger, often moving off-screen.

stashapp/stash.title: De-duplicating auto-taggable strings
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Autotag builds regexes of Tag names, Tag aliases, Studio names, Studio aliases, and Performer names. We currently do only the most rudimentary matching, which leads to problems. Having two performers, "Jane" and "Jane Doe", will match both. There are many complaints of 'single name performers' causing problems. Tag aliases currently allow many different tags to match against the same string.

⚠️ This is a blocker for a conversion of Performer aliases from freeform comma separated text to auto-taggable individual entries.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We create regexes with a small subset of regex features, and they are generated deterministically and predictably. When creating a tag name, tag alias, performer name, studio, or studio alias, we should perform a check to see if the generated regex either describes a regular language that is a sub- or super-set of the language described by the regex generated by another token. This is called the "regex inclusion problem" in the literature, although implementations are few and far between.

Regex inclusion will probably require implementing this as a libr

stashapp/stash.title: Phash validation
stashapp/stash.body:
**Describe the bug**
We recently started using phashes for matching against StashDB. This has exposed bugs in the phash generation process.  A broken or unparsable file will result in common phashes, which will then be matched to a random scene in StashDB that has had that same broken phash uploaded. We may not be able to fix the underlying ffmpeg issues, but we can work around them. During phash generation / use, we should validate to make sure the phash doesn't match a known bad phash ( results of solid color, color bars, etc.), and other phash validation rules.

Further investigation is still needed, but I've identified some facts already:
Real phashes should have a (roughly?) even amount of 1s and 0s
Many bad phashes 'look' strange. They have slow entropy.
If ffmpeg determines that the video duration is zero, the phash is almost always junk.

Known bad phashes so far:
(note, they may vary in the wild by 1-3 bits, so checks should check for a hamming-distance match)
```
a000000000800080
8080808080808080
870707030787fefc
82070707078ffff8
8055557555575575
805555555d755d55
87070707037ef8fc
8707070303fefcdc
cdcdcdc9c1233332
```

        location = /deovr {

stashapp/stash.title: i18n: Streamline Singular/Plural Nouns
stashapp/stash.body:
<!-- Update or delete the title if you need to delegate your title gore to something
# Title

*### Scope*
<!-- describe the scope of your topic and your goals ideally within a single paragraph or TL;DR kind of summary so its easier for people to determine if they can contribute at a glance. -->
TL;DR; the localization table is a mess right now with singulars and plurals being thrown all over the place - maybe it's time to do some cleanup.

##  Long Form
Back when i18n was first implemented, a lot of the terminologies were put under the root key of the localization table. As the project has grown, more and more string categories were created. Now we have a *somewhat* clean section for translators to figure out what the context of the string may be based on the key ID (e.g., `actions.add` -> verb form of `add` might be used, as opposed to noun). 

The problem now is that some of these "legacy" strings are now littering the root section of the localization table, with most of them being nouns that cannot be appropriately placed due to the generic nature of the terms. There are now some implementations use `countables.<entity_type>` or just `<entity_type>/<entity_type>s`.

2. Made a new operation just to calculate the Phash and return it.
3. Change the order of generate/hook.

 - New: Scan > Generate > Hook Plugin

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

That’s a bit of an involved example of course. In my case I’m wanting to do something simple like [Rating, Random] but I include

stashapp/stash.title: Resume Interrupted Task Queue
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If a task is interrupted (for example by an automatically triggered Docker update), the existing queue is lost and has to be rebuilt from scratch.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Persist some data indicating what’s in the queue, and what has been done / needs to be done in the current task. If the task is interrupted then it can pick up where it left off in the current task, and keep any queued up tasks in the queue. 

Should there be a schema update between when the task is interrupted and when it resumes the queue should stay the same, but the interrupted task should start from the beginning. This avoids resuming a task that may not be compatible with the new schema. This should be a noted effect that’s explained on the scheme migration page that’s presented before the migration starts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
The addition of the task queue is great, and this would help take it to the next level.

Add the ability to rate your tags in the same manner as all other media and objects. This includes enabling the ability to both sort and filter tags by star ratings.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None needed as this already has precedence in the rest of the objects and media.

**Additional context**
With everything else having the ability to be rated now, Tags appear to be the last holdouts. I went through everything else I could find and I believe it’s all able to be rated!

stashapp/stash.title: Semantic FUSE filesystem to mount organised version of contents of library in host filesystem
stashapp/stash.body:

I'd like my files to be tidy and navigable on my filesystem but I don't want Stash to make destructive edits to my files.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to see a semantic FUSE filesystem implemented in Stash.

I feel a bit gauche making a feature request that's "I want this thing from this other software in your software" but I've not seen it in anything else. I use a tool which in addition to its main use offers this feature for music files it manages. The tool is made for and only compatible with a private community but the code is open source under MIT, also happens to be written in Go, and available to view [here](https://gitlab.com/passelecasque/varroa).

 Here's the author describing the feature:

>Varroa can serve a read-only [semantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_file_system) FUSE filesystem that can be mounted in an existing empty folder. It will automatically organize and let you explore releases using the metadata retrieved with Varroa.
>
> The mount point will display:
> 
> ```
>     artists/
>     format/
>     record labels/
>     source/
>     tags/

stashapp/stash.title: Extend Performer/Scene Tagger for other scrapers
stashapp/stash.body:

Right now, if URLs are set for various scenes or performers, it is not possible to scrape them in bulk. You have to manually scrape each one. The UI is very useful, so it would be nice to be able to leverage it for other scrapers as well.

For performers, it would be nice to be able to search for performers (like you can with individual scrapers) in the same way the "Untagged" update currently works on the tagger. Additionally, refresh could be leveraged to reupdate various fields utilizing other scrapers. I guess the problem is that there is only one URL field, but multiple performer scrapers that can be run.

For scenes, there's no real search option unless integration with TPDB is added (which is out of the scope of this feature), so if a URL is set, then only should it be available for scraping/tagging. This one does not matter to me as much, but I imagine there are others out there that may find it useful.
