stashapp/stash.title: Contextual filtering across all objects
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Tags is one of the major ways you sort the content besides Performer and Studio. Its therefore inefficient to hide the tags under dropdown. Dropdown means it takes atleast two clicks and you scroll the tags in list form. This is fine for less used items like Country, Path etc

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I want tags to be available as a 'Tag Cloud' atleast while I'm on important pages (Performer, Studio). It'll make the filtering that much more efficient. The tags cloud should not display redundant tags. 

If Tag Cloud has large tags to display, let it show atleast the 'most used' 8 to 10 tags in cloud form, while the remaining accessible in drop-down arrow beside it.

Lets Suppose: 
**Performer 1** has  _Tag1_, _Tag2_. 
**Performer 2**  tags _Tag3_, _Tag4_.
**Studio 1** has  _Tag5_, _Tag6_.
**Studio 2** has  _Tag7_, _Tag8_.
So, if I apply filter and my page is displaying only '**Performer 2 + Studio 1**', then the tag cloud should only show _Tag3, Tag4, Tag5, Tag6_.

Having the tags visible allows to see the tag content of the selection at a glance while also aiding in its further filtering,

stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In Stash you typically start in some kind of collection. It may be a gallery, a studio, the scenes page, etc. As soon as you select an individual piece of media though, you’re kicked out of the collection and in to a very isolated page. In order to view any other media in the collection you have to pop back out, select a new item, then end up back in an isolated page.

stashapp/stash.title: Filter the stash-box query based on existing metadata
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Searching with generic terms could lead to ambiguous results. If I search for "2018-01-01 StudioXX", I also get results for a studio named "StudioXX YY". I know that the particular scene is from "Studio "XX", so the search could be narrowed to by enriching the query with existing metadata. The metadata (i.e. the Studio) would have been set manually in this case for the scene without stashbox id

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The tagger configuration should have options to filter the stash-box query based on existing metadata. This could be two checkboxes "Filter based on Studio" and "Filter based on Performer".

When the boxes are ticked an I perform a query, stash checks if the particular scene is associated with a studio and/or performer(s) that has a stash-id. If this is the case the query is modified accordingly.

The stashbox api could be changed like that:

From

```graphql
searchScene(term: String!, limit: Int): [Scene!]!
````

To:

```graphql
input SearchFilterInput {
  studio_id: ID
  performer_ids: [ID!]
}
searchScene(term: String!, limit: Int, filter: SearchFilterInput):

You might have a 10 second long gif and a 5 second silent video clip. As far as the user is concerned they are more or less the same thing. If anything the longer gif is more video like. This means you can view those gifs with the nice lightbox feature in the wall layout of the Image view but you wouldn't be able to with those short clips. That is one situation where you might want to see both Scenes and Images together but there a variety of different situations where that would be useful. For example you might want to quickly see all images and videos from a particular performer. Being able to pull that up in a single view could be quite nice.

However there are some times (such as the case where you have a mix of gifs and clips) where it would be good to see all me

stashapp/stash.title: Folder-like structure for organizing content
stashapp/stash.body:

The user is essentially presented with one big flat list which is filterable and sortable and such but does not offer any visualising of that original folder structure. When it comes to the experience of browsing though your videos Stash essentially says each video in the list is of roughly equal independent value to you. But sometimes you have a set or collection of particular videos in which you would like to be presented with the collection when browsing though the Scenes view but which you don't necessarily want every video in that collection filling up that list.

## Detailed description of issue
Say you've got a Stash db filled with a modest sized number of nicely tagged videos that you know you'd be roughly equality interested in watch any of them. You can pull up the scenes tab and browse though and you see a broad variety of videos allowing you to find something that takes your fancy at that current moment. The current flat hierarchy system works perfectly fine here. 

But then say you wanted to import a folder (or number of folde

stashapp/stash.title: Stash built for a particular type of conventual studio-produced porn, management of porn outside that could be improved
stashapp/stash.body:
## Summary
Stash is currently build primarily for porn produced by a studio. As such it has patchy support for any porn that falls outside of this. I would love to see what peoples thinking about this is and ideally for support to improve over time or at least to make that this implicit focus more transparent in Stash's marketing.

##  Detailed description
For the purposes of this discussion I'm going to focus mostly on video although this definitely applies to images too, maybe to a lesser extend. I use the word "video" but Stash doesn't really have the notion of a generic video (at least in terms of the interface presented to the user). Instead stash has "Scenes" which can make up "Movies" which are concepts that are applicable for a particular type of porn. By catering specifically for porn that fits within this paradigm you can make more targeted assumptions about what sort of metadata is applicable. "Scenes" have a scene number from the "Movie" that they are a part of. "Movies" are made by "Studios". Etc etc. 

This has a bunch of advantages. With more specific metadata which you can assume to be broadly applicable for all media that is stored you can present a richer UI

stashapp/stash.title: Allow to change encoder for FFmpeg -c:v parameter in Configuration for Preview Generation
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Very slow CPU bound preview encoding while generating support files.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Assuming that 99% of us are using AMD or NVIDIA GPUs, a dropdown on the Stash configuration screen under Preview Generation to select the desired encoder for preview videos to change the parameter of the underlying FFmpeg command from the default setting to one of the following:

stashapp/stash.title: Log potential issues with files and show in dedicated information hub
stashapp/stash.body:
When scanning files we discard a lot of information that could be used to quickly identify issues or improve a collection.

Examples include:
* Corrupted files
* Wrong filenames (ts container with mp4 extension)
* Inappropriate containers (h264 stream in ts container, needlessly requiring transcode)
* Pointless gallery compression
* Duplicate files

We could save a lot of tech support by logging this info and putting it in an easily searchable view which quickly lets the user know why something does not work as expected.

It could be as simple as a scene_warnings table with id/string that we push to while scanning, and a tab in settings which displays the table, with a more expanded explanation of the issue.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like a configuration option that lets me specify the number of ffmpeg threads I want to use. The default could still be 4 if the configuration option isn't specified.

**Additional context**
This is similar to https://github.com/stashapp/stash/issues/818, but that issue is more broad in scope. Also, running a single instance of ffmpeg with more threads makes better use of resources (disk, CPU cache, etc.) on some machines than multiple instances. This would also be easier to implement.

All the web sites follow the same structure, except they use a different base url (such as `www.google.com` or `www.duckduckgo.com`). Sometimes when scraping for the image on these sites it's impossible to get anything but the relative url, (such as `/image/thumb.gif`).

If our scraper were only ever dealing with one web site, we could hard code the base url for the image in post-processing, but when dealing with multiple sites, there's no way for our scraper to know which of the sites we're dealing with so we cannot hard code the base url.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Either,

1. Create a constant, such as $domain, that contains the value of the base url that is being scraped based off the url being scraped. So if the scene provided is http://www.domain.com/videos/scene.html, then $domain would contain `http://www.domain.com`, or

2. A more flexible solution (assuming it's feasible and doesn't break anything), allow post-processing for common fields so users can just make their own custom variables contain

stashapp/stash.title: Automated client-side update mechanism
stashapp/stash.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am often remote from my server, so if Stash has an update, I am unable to install it until I am back with the server. This is because the current update flow requires grabbing the latest binary, shutting Stash down, copying it over the existing one, and starting Stash back up. There is no client-side update mechanism.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Ideally, this would be a two phase approach

1. Create an update mechanism that allows updates to be manually triggered on the UI and completed silently. Essentially, automating the steps above for downloading the new binary in a temporary location, shutting down Stash, replacing the binaries from the temp dir (need another update process that does not get shut down for this), deleting the temp dir, and starting up the main process again.

2. Once above works, it could be feasible to allow users to configure updates to be installed automatically without any intervention. This can help users stay up to date without having to follow when releases are made. I think while the first development is fairly common in most modern applications, this option is not a

stashapp/stash-box.title: [RFC] Studio Founding and Closure Dates + Defunct Status
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Draft: for discussion, not implementation-ready.

### Scope
Studios currently don't have founding/closure dates. Occasionally, users have to vote "no" erroneous removals because the link isn't accessible anymore, mainly due to being unclear the studio is defunct. The studio profiles could have some more metadata attached to them to mitigate this. The immediate fields that come to mind are:
+ Status: Starter statuses of Active/Defunct. This level of detail shows a voter more info that they link they're about to click on might not work if it's defunct.
+ Founding Date/Year: The date when the studio was incorporated or the release date of its XXX001 scene. Nice info to have, many metadata sources have this.
+ Closure Date/Year: The date when the studio stopped operating/went offline permanently, or became effectively defunct. Nice to have in the case of seeing defunct and knowing for how long.

### Out of scope
Without making this overly complex, there are cases where acquisitions under a different alias could constitute to a "new" start date. Probably too in the weeds, but that's the holy grail of metadata around studios. 

Real life example:
+ 2011 to 2020: AussiesDoIt was an indepe

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Bug Report] Unclear error message for email cooldown
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Describe the bug**
Apparently Stash-Box has a five minute cooldown period before it will send another email to the same address. However it's not clear to use that's what's happening because the error message says "pending-email-change". This sounds more like the user requested to change their email address and the error won't go away until that process is resolved one way or another.

This became an issue recently when a user complained of being blocked from resetting their password on a brand-new account. I believe what happened was they created the account with a mis-typed password, couldn't log in afterward, and tried to trigger a password reset within 5 minutes of receiving the registration email. Not knowing what the problem was, they reached out to me.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new account
2. Immediately ask for password reset
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
Clearer and more helpful error message, warning the user that the cooldown is active and they just have to wait a few minutes before trying again.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [RFC] Removing OSHASH
stashapp/stash-box.body:
## Scope
The OSHASH fingerprint type should be removed from stash-box which should instead focus on PHASH and perhaps other, newer algorithms

##  Reasoning
The primary function of the stash-box database as it relates to Stash is the ability to match your local videos to their canonical metadata as served by the studio or network that released it. It is a community-driven database that matches fingerprints generated by your local Stash against those submitted by the community of users for that particular stash-box.

The two types of fingerprint used by both stash and stash-box are PHASH (perceptual hash) and OSHASH (Open Subtitle Hash), but they have very different uses: the perceptual hash allows for "fuzzy matching" because similar scenes will have a similar hash, independent of factors like resolution and watermarks, while the OSHASH is closer to a cryptographic hash and is sensitive to any changes to the first and last 64k of the file.

The main benefit of the OSHASH is that it is arguably more accurate than PHASH: if you've downloaded a new scene from a studio and not altered it in any way, it's very likely that your OSHASH will match the same file downloaded by anyone else in

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Bug Report] Fingerprint edit filter masked by favorites
stashapp/stash-box.body:
## Description

Filtering notifications by `FINGERPRINTED_SCENE_EDIT` returns no results for edits to scenes where I have submitted fingerprints, if I have also favorited the relevant performer or studio.

## Steps to Reproduce

Assuming there's a pending edit to a scene for which you have submitted fingerprints, and the scene contains a favorited performer or is from a favorited studio:
1. Go to the Notifications page and filter by **"An edit to a scene you have submitted fingerprints for."**
2. Observe: no results returned, even though a matching notification exists.
3. Switch the filter to **"An edit to a performer you have favorited"** (or **All**).
4. Observe: the notification appears.

## Expected Behavior

The notification should appear when filtering by `FINGERPRINTED_SCENE_EDIT`.

## Actual Behavior

The notification only appears under `FAVORITE_PERFORMER_EDIT` or `FAVORITE_STUDIO_EDIT`. Filtering by `FINGERPRINTED_SCENE_EDIT` returns nothing.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Bug Report] Deleted fields in edits are reset when updating the edit
stashapp/stash-box.body:
This affects production ([v0.5.3](https://github.com/stashapp/stash-box/releases/tag/v0.5.3)), as well as current develop.

#### **To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Existing performer with (for example) height set to 170 cm.
2. Make an edit to remove the height, and modify (change/add, but not delete) at least one other field.
3. Click to update the edit.
4. Height is silently restored to the form field.
When the update is submitted, the deleted value is restored to the edit.

_**This is applicable to at least height and disambiguation, but likely others, and on other entities too.**_

#### **Expected behavior**
Deleted fields in an edit to carry over when updating the edit.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Add backend support for AutoCrop for automated headshots
stashapp/stash-box.body:
## Proposal summary
Integrate [Autocrop](https://github.com/leblancfg/autocrop) into the stash-box backend to automatically crop existing and newly added photos, into consistent headshots.

## What is Autocrop

Autocrop is a Python tool, both from the command line and as a Python API, utilizing OpenCV, designed to automatically detect and crop faces from images, centering the output around the largest detected face. 

## Benefits of integrating Autocrop with stash-box

- **Enhanced Visuals.** Headshots improve clarity when performer images are displayed in smaller formats, such as thumbnails and dropdown selects.
- **User Curation of Crops Via Voting Or Moderator Selection.** Not all automated headshots will be of quality, as this is primarily dependent on the source image. Users, moderators, or admins could select which headshots to use and which to discard either through voting or administrative override.
- **Consistency.** Automating this process ensures consistent cropping for all images into headshots. Users curated headshots will never be as consistent without the strict use of templates and rigid quality assurance oversight of submissions.
- **DMCA compliance.**

stashapp/stash-box.body:
### Scope
My proposal is to add namespaces/sources to tags, like "Some Site / Tag Name", to preserve their original (and possibly distinct) meanings. These tags should then be mapped to the StashDB tags by dynamic parent/sub-tag relationships, like the ones in Stash.

## Long Form
The main problem with tags from different sources is that they could easily mean different things. For example, "Medium Ass" could have a precise numerical meaning on one site, and be much more fuzzy on another. This makes the whole tag's meaning much more fuzzy if these different tags are treated as the same one.

As far as I can tell, currently this problem is solved by mapping the source tags to more appropriate StashDB ones when importing the metadata. This requires some level of expertise, for each tag on the site, from the one doing the importing, at the time of import and ultimately makes the process more difficult and slow. And without expertise or care, or by mistake, it pollutes the meaning of existing tags.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [RFC] Improved edit count calculation; current method is flawed
stashapp/stash-box.body:
## Problem

Currently, accepted edit counts serve primarily as a metric for gauging a user's trustworthiness and participation. However, in the context of proposed leaderboards and/or gamification (see #417, #569), the existing method of calculating edits should be recalibrated to increase accuracy and mitigate manipulation.

### Accuracy
The current method of calculating accepted edits falls short of accurately reflecting a user's contributions. A submission where only one field changed is equal to a submission where where the maximum amount of possible fields has changed. That is, all successful submissions are equal to *1 edit point*, regardless of how many fields within that submission were effected.

### Manipulation

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Bug Report] Downscaled Studio Logos Lose Transparency
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Weird that we didn't have this one written up yet, but it appears this is still an issue. I'm not familiar with the specifics of the relevant code here but this is my understanding of what's causing this problem.

**Describe the bug**
Practically every studio image uploaded to the database will be a PNG file of a logo on a transparent background. If the image is too large (greater than 1280px in either dimension), Stash-Box automatically downscales the image into a JPG. Because it's no longer a PNG, the transparency is lost and replaced with a black background. It does the same for performer and scene images but transparency isn't an issue for those two. 

**Expected behavior**
The current downscaling process is perfectly fine for every other object type, studios are the only issue. Downscaling into a PNG instead of a JPG would only be useful for the studio images so we would only need to alter the process for studios. We can leave the others alone and maintain the smaller file sizes using the current level of compression for those JPGs.

**Screenshots**
Courtesy of DogmaDragon's recent test:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64123896/219466682-249f9c9e-1

# Collect more info with file hashes (fingerprints)

## Scope
### OHASHs
OHASHs seem to have limited usefulness when it comes to identifying scenes after PHASHs were added, to make OSHASHs potentially more useful I would suggest tracking the container, vertical resolution, and file size associated with the hash, these attributes could provide more insight into bad submissions as well as potentially useful information about a scene/studio size in terms of storage.

### PHASHs
PHASHs have the potential to be applied to the wrong scene with little to no way to tell besides comparing to other submissions or the associated duration a solution to this could be submitting a scene scrubber sprite along with each unique PHASH this would make it easier to identify incorrect matches using standardized screenshots generated by the stash client

stashapp/stash-box.title: Update performer unique name constraint
stashapp/stash-box.body:
The performers table's unique name constraint should be updated to account for `NULL` disambiguation, and gender:
```sql
DROP INDEX "index_active_performers_on_name";

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "index_active_performers_on_name"
  ON "performers" ("name", COALESCE("disambiguation", ''), "gender")
  WHERE NOT "deleted";
```

List dupes that will block this migration:
```sql
SELECT P.*
FROM performers P
JOIN (
	SELECT unnest(array_agg(id)) AS id
	FROM performers
	WHERE deleted = FALSE
	GROUP BY (name, COALESCE(disambiguation, ''), gender)
	HAVING count(*) > 1
) T ON T.id = P.id
ORDER BY P.name ASC;
```

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Ability to remove incorrect fingerprints from scenes
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
Stash's tagger may match scenes incorrectly due to incorrect fingerprints associated with scenes on stash-box.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make it possible to remove incorrect hashes directly in stash-box. In addition, when a new scene is added with hashes that already belong to another scene, one could ask the user to automatically file a removal of the incorrect hashes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep using the backlog spreadsheet, which is inefficient.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Disallow the submission of thumbnails generated by stash
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
Some of the scenes submitted by the democracy use the automatically generated thumbnails by stash, not the official thumbnail.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Stash-box should detect that the thumbnail is bogus and remove it from the draft and warn the user that the thumbnail has been removed.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Make it possible to mark performers as ambiguous
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
A lot of ambiguous performers (e.g. Maria) have bogus metadata attached to them, such as birthdate, eye color, images of disambiguated performers and so forth.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make it possible to mark performers as ambiguous. Once they are marked as ambiguous, all metadata fields will become locked, disallowing the addition of nonsensical metadata. Also, in the search results, the match should indicate that the performer is indeed ambiguous and should display the performer as Maria (Ambiguous).

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Add the ability to search through edits
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
Currently, it is not possible to search among the edits, except from using the basic filters. A simple text search would be useful to find edits of interest.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Initially a simple free text search field that can search through edits in the title field, performer fields and studio field. In later versions, it would be nice to have more granular filters that we can save.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I've been using the favorite feature very primitively, I mark the studio of interest, look through the edits, then unfavorite the studio again.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Ability to upload multiple images for studios
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Studios can have multiple logos and sizes: landscape, square, wordmarks, favicon, etc. Some logos also change over time. Please add the ability to upload more than one image per studio.

Bonus if the images can have labels, such as "landscape" for landscape logos and "square" for 1:1 aspect radio images.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [RFC] Performer Image Categorization
stashapp/stash-box.body:
## Scope
There is a significant desire to better organize performer images on stash-box, particularly by allowing images to be categorized by crop, pose, and state of dress.

## Problem
Stash-Box performer images are currently organized by resolution only, basically serving the highest resolution image first followed by the rest in descending order. More popular performers can have many images and our StashDB guidelines encourage a diverse set for each performer representing various crops, poses, states of dress, and general "looks" from the performer's career. Typically, users will prefer a particular type of performer image for their personal use and are often left navigating stash-box's image carousel one-by-one until they find the "best" image. Currently, the only way to set a default image for a particular performer in stash-box is by making sure the preferred image has a higher resolution then the rest of the set. This is an imperfect work-around that requires maintaining a hard cap on image resolution for each performer rather than a true solution.

##  Proposal
The implementation of image categories could help to alleviate these issues. If individual images can be ta

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Multiple-select field values (breast type, ethnicity, nationality, etc)
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A few fields would be more accurately represented with the capacity to have multiple values. This is related to #210 and expands upon it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add multi-value support for:

1. Ethnicity
Applicable performer's could have combos like `Asian` and `Black` to accurately reflect them, instead of falling into one of the other or into `Mixed`, which seems like a catch-all for unknown mixed ethnicity.
2. Breast type
Many performers start their career with natural and change to augmented. How can we better reflect that?
a. Allowing multiple values
b. Allowing multiple values with an adjacent form for date ranges (i.e. "Natural, 2010 - 2015; Augmented: 2015 - 2019")
3. Nationality
Somewhat of an edge case, but there are performer's that have dual nationalities. This would apply to people who are born in country a, but raised and are a citizen of country b. This is really pedantic but I thought I'd mention it for accuracy's sake.
4. Hair color
See #210

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Amending edits
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Implement the option to amend/update already-submitted edits, prior to their application/rejection.
This will help immensely in resolving conflicts (when they are identified ahead of time), correcting mistakes (typos, missing/incorrect data, switching merge direction, updating merge sources) and generally updating data due to a comment from a fellow user.
Currently the only option is to cancel and recreate the edit.

A preliminary design idea - use the entity forms (`PerformerForm`, `SceneForm`, `TagForm`, `StudioForm`).
This is open to suggestions. 

- [x] By default, the form will be populated with the edit details, merged with the entity's current values - current value, unless edit details is not null for that field (edit details override entity's current values).
- [ ] Have the option to reset specific fields to the entity's current values.
- [x] "Confirm" tab should diff the new values, either against the entity's current values, or against the edit's current details (this might be too confusing).
- [x] ~~Will require some changes to the components in order to allow passing all the "old" values (edit's `old_details`).~~
	Perhaps this will not be needed - if the "Confirm" tab

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Lock fields
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Eventually Stashbox is going going to encounter cases of vandalism or a lot of good faith bad edits on the same recurring fields of data. While all edits require approval, the pending edits will still clutter the queue. I think this is where locked fields can be useful. 

[TMDB](https://www.themoviedb.org/bible/general/59f792a29251413e93000001#59f793929251413e93000010) defines locked fields as,

>Confirmed data is routinely locked by content moderators. Moderators may also lock data to prevent vandalism.
>When you stumble upon incorrectly locked data, please use the report button, explain the problem and link us to a proper source if needed.

Locked fields are indicated by a padlock icon next to the field. Unlocked fields are indicated by an open padlock next to the field.

- Depending on the type of headshot the user selects, 1/4 headshot, 1/2 headshot, etc referenced here #211, the above guide will change to suit the headshot style.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Make the hair color field a multi-value field
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A lot of performers use a different hair color throughout their career, but only allowing one option limits us to just one hair color. If Jane Doe has brown hair in three scenes, and blond hair in three scenes, her hair color should be defined as both blond and brown.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make the hair color field a multi-value field. That is, let a performer have more than one hair color.

**Additional context**
I'm not sure if the `various` option is applicable here or if it's for performers that have multi-colored hair. Either way, it would be really vague to select `various` for every performer that has used different hair colors throughout their content.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Add penis size, for male and trans performers
stashapp/stash-box.body: Should function similarly to measurement fields in that it's hidden for "incompatible" genders.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Add performer shoe size
stashapp/stash-box.body: Shoe size is a static property that should be relatively low effort to add. The only question is whether to pick US or EU sizes.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Add image categorization
stashapp/stash-box.body:
To support user preferences and different use cases for images, we should add image categorization.
* Resolution: 2/3, 16/9, etc.
* Crop: Bust, full body, three quarters, etc.
* Orientation: Front, side, back, etc.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Add the posibility to order performer images
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Right now, images are solely sorted by the image resolution. This is undesirable, the resolution of an image does not determine its quality. Some images may have a high resolution, but are in fact grainy. Also, the primary image may be unflattering or might not be the desired choice as performer card image.

This can be resolved by allowing users to upvote images and ordering them by the number of votes. The images that haven't received any votes remain ordered by resolution.

stashapp/stash-box.body:
# Problem

Need to provide a native data import process which handles mapping to other options. The process should allow for the creation of complete scene data without needing to perform post-import modifications.

# Proposal

This RFC is based on the previous work in the branch at https://github.com/InfiniteTF/stash-box/tree/bulk-import

Here is the basic requirements I think are needed for the mvp import functionality:
* accept csv (json to come later)
* support mapping of csv columns to scene fields
* support fixed scene fields (not just studio)

* user navigates to the import page

* system parses the file, inserting the data into a database table, and attempts to match studio/tag/performer names to objects
* system presents the results and allows the user to map/change studio/tag/performer names from the data to actual object instances (using auto-complete selectors)

stashapp/stash-box.title: [RFC] More user roles
stashapp/stash-box.body:
Having users use the shared test account is less than ideal, and I figure that we don't want to open up registration too much.

Propose adding the following user roles:
* `FINGERPRINT_READ` - allows querying for fingerprints only - plus the minimum operations for the user control panel to work. 
* `FINGERPRINT_SUBMIT` - implies `FINGERPRINT_READ`, allows for submission of fingerprints.

Propose also that configuration should include default roles when a user registers without an invite code.

In practise, I see envision the following:
* open up free registration without invite code, allowing for fingerprint reading and possibly submitting
* maintain the existing invite code system, which assigns more broader roles

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Query URL/Request Scrape
stashapp/stash-box.body:
We should be able to query urls on the site and if not found, it should have an option to request a scrape. 
The Scraping system should be automatic with its own work queue for missing scenes. Ofc it should only scrape sites it supports. 
Doing something like this, gives the users an alternative to find the scene they want if they found it somewhere else. 
Also allows users to easily add scenes and all the metadata without manual input and mistakes which is safer in the end.

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Studio Logo's/Images
stashapp/stash-box.body:
If we could host Logo's and images for the studios with support for maybe multiple / set one as default (rating based maybe?)
Then the stash clients could pull the image easily when needed.

This would also remove the manual legwork everyone needs to do to make it look nice, sharing the load of these logos would be good.
Also would be a way to share custom logos someone might make in different styles or looks like a shared unified color style. 

EDIT:
These uploads should support SVG vector files as they are lossless and scale to any size and is really small... though limited to many different colors. 
This way users could trace bad image files from sites and made clean and sharp vectors that scale to any size and need you want!

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Changelog on StashDB for bulk activity and site/network additions
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Describe the solution you'd like**
I had an idea on the Discord that the StashDB site should have a Changelog section, where you can track bulk changes to the database, and also with site/network additions. Perhaps also error correction too? Thus allowing users to know when to scrape/re-scrape certain network/sites/performers. Example below:-

13/05/2021 - Linked X-Art Performer Aliases to Parent Performers
12/05/2021 - Added PornHub (MadeInCanarias)

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Feature] Share Markers via Stash-Box
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Importing markers into stash at the moment is a bit of a hassle, it would be nice to be able to do this automatically from stash-box, this sort of crowd sourcing of metadata seems to be the exact purpose of stash-box

**Describe the solution you'd like**
share markers with an associated phash/oshash/scene_duration, that could then be imported on scrape from a stash instance

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Scraping markers from various sites and creating corresponding markers via stash's graphql interface, this works but doing this via stash-box seems like a better solution and could benefit from crowd sourcing

stashapp/stash-box.title: [Bug Report] Fields updated to NULL are ignored
stashapp/stash-box.body:
**Describe the bug**
Whenever a mutation is sent to modify a value to NULL, the column is ignored and the old value is retained. This makes it impossible to set values to Unknown.

stashapp/stash-box.title: Traefik Reverse Proxy for Dev instance
stashapp/stash-box.body: We're going to want a front end load balancer and reverse proxy so that we can deploy and test the API directly on http and via https.  I would almost go as far as to suggest that the API should not operate in plaintext but that's up to @WithoutPants and @InfiniteTF to discuss how that'll work.
